Domain.description: The architecture domain or domains that the demand relates to: Business, Data, Application, Technology or Security (interfaces and integration belong to Application). It decides the owner of the demand.
Domain.how_to_resolve:
1. Read the business need, the expected outcome, and the systems and data mentioned in the demand.
2. Check each named system, data set and platform against the Application Catalog, Data Catalog, Technology Catalog and Security Control Catalog to see which domain it belongs to.
3. Choose the main domain and write it first, based on the majority of the content. Add other domains only when the demand clearly needs them.
4. Add Security when the data is Confidential or Restricted (check the Data Classification Standard), or the demand touches sign-in, encryption or security controls.
5. Record the business domain (the department that asks) separately, not in this field.
Domain.where_to_look:
• Standard intake question Q4 (which architecture domains)
• Demand list: business need, systems or data mentioned, data sensitivity (optional field)
• Application Catalog, Data Catalog, Technology Catalog and Security Control Catalog: to see which domain a system, application or data entity belongs to
• Architecture Principles and Standards: to check data classification and other domain constraints such as Cloud and Hosting
Domain.rules:
Valid domains and what each covers (exactly five):
• Business: processes, services, policies, organization, capabilities and people
• Data: any area that comes under the data domain in TOGAF and similar frameworks, for example data sources, analytics, reports, data quality, data sharing and data classification
• Application: any area that comes under the application, system and platform domain in TOGAF and similar frameworks, for example applications for business users, and the interfaces and integration between applications, modules and system features
• Technology: any area that comes under the infrastructure and technology domain in TOGAF and similar frameworks, for example infrastructure, cloud, hosting, network and data center
• Security: a new or changed security control or security capability. Controls can be sign-in and access, encryption, monitoring or protection of Confidential or personal data (for example, multi-factor sign-in for the staff portal)
Main domain first. Integration is not a domain: interfaces and integration belong to Application. Business domains (Human Resources, Finance, Customer Services and others) are not values of this field.
Domain.examples:
Correct: Application; Security for the employee mobile app (a new app that connects to the HR system and payroll through interfaces and holds Confidential employee data).
Wrong: Human Resources (a business domain, not an architecture domain), or Integration (not a domain).
Domain.info_needed: The demand names no system or data and the need is unclear. Ask which systems or data are involved.
Domain.info_needed_source: The routing matrix has no domain for the topic, or the catalogs do not list the system. Say so and ask the EA Office.

Impacted application.description: The existing applications, platforms and tools that the demand would change, connect to, replace or depend on, taken from the Application Catalog.
Impacted application.how_to_resolve:
1. Read the systems and data named in the demand and in the answers to the intake questions.
2. Match each name to the Application Catalog, using the glossary and aliases (for example, 'the HR app' is the Peoplex HR system, C-204).
3. Add applications that exchange data with the matched ones when the demand needs that data (Application Interaction Diagram, Data Flow Diagram, Data to Application Matrix).
4. List the main application first, with its catalog ID or contract ID.
5. Use the analysis from this step to show, in the screening observation, how the application links to the other domain artefacts and components (Data Catalog, Application to Technology Matrix, Application to Security Control Matrix).
Impacted application.where_to_look:
• Standard intake question Q7 (systems or data involved)
• Application Catalog: names, IDs, owner roles and lifecycle status
• Application Interaction Diagram and Application Landscape Diagram: connected applications
• Application Interface Catalog: interfaces and APIs of the matched applications
• Application to Technology Matrix and Infrastructure Landscape Diagram: the platforms they run on
• Application to Security Control Matrix: the controls that protect them
• Demand list: systems or data mentioned
• Initiative portfolio: 'Systems affected' of running and planned projects
Impacted application.rules:
• Link by a name match (through the catalog). Never link by department alone.
• A solution that does not exist yet is not listed here. Describe it in the observation.
Impacted application.examples:
Correct: 'HR system (Peoplex, C-204); payroll; attendance devices' for the leave and attendance app.
Wrong: 'HR' or 'the mobile app' (a department, and a system that does not exist yet).
Impacted application.info_needed: The demand names no system or data. Ask which systems or data are involved.
Impacted application.info_needed_source: The Application Catalog has no matching entry or is out of date. Write 'not in data' and ask the Lead Application Architect.

Duplicate with existing artefact.description: The existing artefact that already covers, or is about to cover, all or part of the need: an application, platform, tool, interface or API, data set, security control, licensed module or project (running, planned or completed). Give the name and the ID, and say what is covered.
Duplicate with existing artefact.how_to_resolve:
1. List what the demand needs: functions, data, interfaces, hosting and security controls.
2. Check each need against the catalogs: the Application Catalog (applications and tools), the Application Interface Catalog (interfaces and APIs), the Data Catalog (data sets and reports), the Technology Catalog (platforms and hosting) and the Security Control Catalog (controls in place).
3. Check the contract register (modules already paid for but not used) and the initiative portfolio (running, planned and completed projects, and future scope that is not yet funded).
4. Write the artefact name and ID, what part of the need it covers and what it does not cover.
5. If nothing matches, write None.
6. Do not recommend reuse here. Whether to reuse it is decided in the Recommendation phase.
Duplicate with existing artefact.where_to_look:
• Standard intake question Q9 (existing application, service, initiative or contract)
• Application Catalog: applications, platforms and tools
• Application Interface Catalog and Application Interface and API Standard: interfaces and APIs
• Data Catalog, Data Dictionary and Data Flow Diagram: data sets, reports and data exchanges
• Technology Catalog and Infrastructure Landscape Diagram: platforms and hosting
• Security Control Catalog: controls in place
• Initiative portfolio: scope summary, 'Reusable outputs (optional)', 'Future scope not yet funded (optional)'
• Contract register: 'Included features not yet used' and 'Notes for reuse'
• Service catalog: standard services and their limits
• Glossary and aliases: official names and IDs
Duplicate with existing artefact.rules:
• Counts: applications, platforms, tools, interfaces and APIs, data sets, security controls, licensed modules not yet activated, and initiatives that are in progress, planned or completed.
• Does not count: a standard service in the service catalog (it makes the request not a demand), or an artefact that only belongs to the same department.
• Always say whether the artefact covers all or part of the need.
• Always give name and ID. If there is no ID, write 'ID not found'.
Duplicate with existing artefact.examples:
Correct: 'C-203 Docuvia workflow engine and e-signature module (licensed, not activated)' for the e-signature demand.
Wrong: 'Document system' (no ID, and nothing about what it covers).
Duplicate with existing artefact.info_needed: The demand does not say which systems are involved. Ask.
Duplicate with existing artefact.info_needed_source: A catalog or the contract register is not available. Write 'artefacts not checked'. Do not write None.

Owners.description: The roles accountable for the capabilities, applications, data, platforms and security controls that the demand impacts. They confirm the impact and receive the demand for review. Roles only, never personal names.
Owners.how_to_resolve:
1. For each impacted application, take the owner role from the Application Catalog or the contract owner role in the contract register.
2. For each impacted capability or service, take the owner role from the Business Capability Map or the Business Service Catalog. If there is none, use the owner of its business domain in the routing matrix.
3. For impacted data, platforms and security controls, take the owner role from the Data Catalog, the Technology Catalog and the Security Control Catalog.
Owners.where_to_look:
• Application Catalog: the owner role of each application
• Business Capability Map and Business Service Catalog: the owner role of each capability and service
• Data Catalog: the data owner and steward
• Technology Catalog: the platform owner
• Security Control Catalog: the control owner
• Organization Structure: units and roles, when an owner role is missing
• Initiative portfolio: 'Project manager role (optional)'
Owners.rules:
Which owner takes precedence (proposed):
• The application owner decides on the application.
• The capability owner decides on the process and the service.
• The data owner decides on the data, and the platform owner on the platform.
• The architecture domain owners review the design. They do not replace the business owner.
The demand coordinator confirms the owners.
Owners.examples:
Correct: 'HR Systems Lead (C-204); Lead Application Architect; Lead Security Architect' for the employee mobile app (the data is Confidential).
Wrong: a personal name, or 'HR Department' (a team, not a role).
Owners.info_needed_source: [PROPOSED by Claude] An owner role is missing from the catalog. Write 'owner not in data' and ask the Head of EA Office. The original had no needs-source line.

Data classification.description: The classification of the data the demand uses, from the Data Classification Standard: Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted.
Data classification.how_to_resolve:
[DRAFT by Claude, EA to confirm]
1. For each data set the demand names, take its classification from the Data Catalog.
2. If a data set is not in the catalog, classify it using the definitions in the Data Classification Standard, and say so.
3. If several data sets are named, the highest classification applies.
4. If the demand names no data, answer Not stated.
Data classification.where_to_look:
• Data Catalog and Data Dictionary: the classification and owner of each data set
• Data Classification Standard: the definition of each level
Data classification.rules:
• Use the exact levels: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted. Not stated when the demand names no data. Not assessed only when the standard is missing.
• Where several data sets are involved, the highest classification applies.
Data classification.examples:
Correct: Confidential, for employee leave and attendance records (the Data Catalog lists them as Confidential).
Wrong: Internal, because the app is only used by staff (the classification belongs to the data, not to who uses it).
Data classification.info_needed: The demand does not say what data it uses. Ask which data sets are involved.
Data classification.info_needed_source: The Data Catalog or the Data Classification Standard is missing. Say which and ask the Head of EA Office.

Linked security capability.description: The security capabilities the demand relies on or must add, at a general level, taken from the Security Control Catalog.
Linked security capability.how_to_resolve:
[DRAFT by Claude, EA to confirm]
1. For each impacted application, take its linked controls from the Application to Security Control Matrix.
2. Add the capabilities that the data classification calls for, using the names in the Security Control Catalog and the Data Classification Standard.
3. Add the capabilities for what the demand touches: sign-in, encryption, monitoring.
4. Use the official capability names. If none applies, write 'No link found'.
Linked security capability.where_to_look:
• Application to Security Control Matrix: the controls linked to each application
• Security Control Catalog: the official capability names
• Data Classification Standard: what each level requires
Linked security capability.rules:
• Use the official names from the Security Control Catalog, not the requester's words.
• Only capabilities supported by a source. 'No link found' is a valid answer.
Linked security capability.examples:
Correct: 'Identity and Access Management; Data Protection' for an app that holds Confidential employee data.
Wrong: 'Firewall' (not a capability in the catalog).
Linked security capability.info_needed_source: The Application to Security Control Matrix or the Security Control Catalog is missing. Say which and ask the Lead Security Architect.
